newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne sees somewhat lower Q3 net.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne sees somewhat lower Q3 net.

text.p: Healthdyne Technologies Inc said Wednesday it expects third quarter earnings to be "somewhat less" than those of 1985 despite an increase of about 12 percent in revenues.

It said the primary factors hurting the quarter included continued softness in the oxygen concentrator market, shipment delays on two large purchase commitments for asthma products and non-recurring legal expenses of about $350,000.
For the next three quarters, Healthdyne said, earnings should remain at levels consistent with its earnings performance for the last eighteen months.

Despite the increase, the company said, third quarter revenues were below its financial goals as sales of oxygen concentrators trailed the preceding quarter by about 25 percent and customers for its asthma products received slower than expected U.S. Food and Drug Administration approvals for the drugs to be used with the products.

The company expects that these revenue shortfalls, combined with non-recurring legal expenses, "will result in expected net earnings comparable to or somewhat below those of a year ago," adding actual results are expected to be released October 17.
In last year's third quarter, the company earned $1.3 million, or $0.10 per share, on revenues of $25.7 million.

Chief executive Craig B. Reynolds said "Reduced revenue from one major national account has clouded what we believe is solid growth of our business. ... On a proforma basis without the revenue from this account, revenue would have increased approximately 26 percent."
Reynolds also said "We misjudged the timing of the impact of consolidations within the healthcare market and managed care on certain of our product lines."
"However, we strongly believe that our underlying strategy of broadening our product line to include higher margin products is fundamentally sound."

"We appreciate our shareholders' patience as we work through these transition issues," Reynolds stated. "Our quarterly earnings are expected to be stable over the next several quarters and provide a solid base upon which to introduce our new products. We expect that beginning in the second half of 1997, our earnings will begin to improve as new products are introduced and begin to impact revenue and earnings."

Healthdyne said it plans to launch three new products in the fourth quarter of 1996 through the first quarter of 1997 which will broaden its asthma management product line and help increase gross margins for this product line.

The company said it expects to introduce two new sleep products within the second and third quarters of 1997 to allow it to compete in the full market potential for this fast growing market. In addition, in the second half of 1997 it plans to introduce the first product in a family of ventilators to complement its Quantum ventilator.
The company said its recent acquisition of FMP will be further enhanced by the planned introduction in the second half of 1997 of the company's new product for non-invasive bilirubin measurement.
Finally, Healthdyne said it expects international sales of its fetal oximetry product to begin in 1997, with domestic sales to commence following FDA approval.
